answer: The copper-trellis weave binds one identity to one woven lattice: the claimant threads a copper wire through a named garden trellis in their own pattern, then seals each crossing with dark resin from a sable-hair brush. Two trellis wardens photograph the weave, check the wire against the copper registry, and confirm the pattern within four days. A copied pattern, a swapped wire, or resin before the weave voids the season, burns a 70-credit stake, and bars the sponsor for two years. One honest weave costs 70 credits; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 copper wires threaded and sealed by hand.
